# BDMV Author vendoring notes

This directory is vendored from the user-supplied GitHub `tsMuxer-master.zip`
snapshot at commit:

`c6b1186209e42c877052e762c9185f3226ef8ea2`

User-supplied ZIP SHA-256:

`248729559b4bc855568014dd0f0419bf72cd191b58807d32d53db49969168e93`

The upstream source is Apache-2.0 licensed; `LICENSE` is retained unchanged.
BDMV Author builds only the `tsmuxer` command-line target and `libmediation`;
the separate tsMuxer GUI source remains present but is not built.

Local integration changes are intentionally narrow and documented:

- raise the old CMake 3.1 compatibility floor to 3.10 to avoid modern CMake
  deprecation warnings;
- make the Git revision probe use the vendored directory and suppress the
  expected error when the source archive has no `.git` directory;
- add a `TSMUXER_VERSION_OVERRIDE` hook so BDMV Author can identify the exact
  vendored snapshot in the private helper binary;
- on Linux, replace hard-coded recursive font-directory scanning with Fontconfig family/style lookup. Generic `sans-serif` is used when no family is specified, and FreeType still performs rendering. This follows the normal NixOS/Linux font configuration instead of assuming `/usr/share/fonts` exists.

Except for the explicitly documented BDMV Author fixes below, upstream muxer/demuxer/codec behavior is retained. The Linux-only Fontconfig integration is confined to subtitle font resolution.


## BDMV Author 0.1.5 native IGS extension

The vendored copy adds `S_HDMV/IGS` as an authoring input. It reuses the graphics stream reader for the simple `IG` timestamp framing generated by BDMV Author, assigns Blu-ray Interactive Graphics stream type `0x91` and PID `0x1400+`, and completes the existing CLPI/MPLS support so Interactive Graphics streams are represented directly in the authored Blu-ray metadata. This replaces BDMV Author's earlier temporary PGS-carrier-and-patch workaround.

## BDMV Author 0.1.63 AVC buffering-period correction

The vendored H.264 `insertSEI` path no longer hard-codes `initial_cpb_removal_delay` to 855000 (9.5 seconds). When tsMuxer must synthesize buffering-period SEI, it derives a 90%-full initial delay from the SPS HRD CPB size and bitrate, using the tighter bound when both NAL and VCL HRD are present. This keeps synthesized timing consistent with the stream's declared HRD model and avoids multi-second AVC title-start stalls on hardware players.
